correctness.rationale: The global reduction is sound. For fixed radius \(r\), central symmetry and convexity give \(\tfrac12 K_c(r)+\tfrac12 K_{-c}(r)\subseteq K_0(r)\); planar Brunn--Minkowski therefore makes the centered disk intersection area-maximal. An \(\varepsilon\)-enclosing disk for an arbitrary measurable set transfers this bound to every positive-area subset. For \(a\le r\le\sqrt2a\), differentiating the exact disk--square area gives \(A'(r)=2r(\pi-4\theta)\), and after \(r=a\sec\theta\), \(x=\pi/2-2\theta\), the derivative sign reduces to the unique zero of \(\cos x-x\). The optimizer contains an antipodal pair at distance \(2r_*\), so its circumradius is exactly \(r_*\). Independent numerical recomputation gives \(\alpha=0.7390851332151607\), \(r_*/a=1.0931697449850168\), and \(\mathcal C_R(Q_1)=0.3094268090583855\), consistent with the analytic proof.
